findings.title: Local account uses reversible or plaintext password storage
findings.description: Cisco 'password' (type 0/7) stores secrets reversibly; 'secret' (type 5/8/9) is hashed. STIG and CIS require hashed secrets exclusively.
findings.explanation: Some local accounts use reversible or plaintext password storage. If the config file is ever copied, backed up or disclosed, these passwords can be recovered immediately. Use the irreversible 'secret' keyword instead.

findings.title: IPsec proposal uses deprecated cryptography
findings.description: DES/3DES, MD5/SHA-1 and DH groups 1-2 are broken or impractical. NIST SC-13 requires AES-256 with SHA-256 and DH group 14 or higher.
findings.explanation: The IPsec proposal uses deprecated cryptography. These primitives are broken or impractical to brute force, so a determined attacker can decrypt captured VPN traffic. Move to AES-256 with a modern authentication hash and Diffie-Hellman group 14 or higher.

findings.title: IPsec proposal uses deprecated cryptography
findings.description: DES/3DES, MD5/SHA-1 and DH groups 1-2 are broken or impractical. NIST SC-13 requires AES-256 with SHA-256 and DH group 14 or higher.
findings.explanation: The IPsec proposal uses deprecated cryptography. These primitives are broken or impractical to brute force, so a determined attacker can decrypt captured VPN traffic. Move to AES-256 with a modern authentication hash and Diffie-Hellman group 14 or higher.
